title: Dynamic grid stabilization, modal stacking resilience, and chart-overflow strategy
creator: Marina Cho
description:
Goal: Harden Redwood Console surfaces (dashboards, rollouts, cost views) against layout shift and cross-browser overflow bugs while keeping a consistent density and accessible interactions. This ticket scopes three related areas: 1) Dynamic grid stabilization — a resilient CSS grid + container-query approach to avoid reflow cascades when charts, tables, or side panels change size; 2) Modal stacking resilience — rules + z-index/container-context fixes so nested dialogs, confirm overlays, and flyouts never trap scroll or clip controls on Safari/iOS and high-DPI Windows; 3) Chart overflow strategy — pragmatic rules for clipping, progressive reveal, or internal scrolling for chart embeddables so we avoid token-costly rerenders and preserve interactivity.

Constraints and trade-offs: we must support customers on older Chromium and Safari versions, ship without a heavy polyfill where feasible, and not regress rendering perf on Dedicated hosts. We prioritized CSS-first solutions (container queries, min/max-inline-size, clamp(), transforms for animation) with small, targeted JS only where browser inconsistencies demand it (e.g., Safari nested overflow workarounds). We evaluated two table strategies: strict virtualization (better perf) vs smart column collapsing (better usability). We chose a hybrid: virtualization for >2k rows and a controlled column-collapse + horizontal scroll for dense tables under 2k rows.

Success criteria (acceptance): 1) No visual overlap or clipped modal controls on supported browsers (Chrome latest, Safari latest, Firefox latest, iPad Safari) on a set of canonical pages; 2) Charts maintain interactive region and do not produce layout thrash when data updates or legends toggle; 3) Table column menus accessible and not truncated at small widths; 4) Automated visual regression baseline added covering 6 breakpoints and modal stacking states; 5) Measured layout-shift score for dashboard pages reduced by >= 40% in Lighthouse lab comparisons.
updates: 2025-11-12: Ticket created after postmortem on rollout dashboard flakiness. Initial audit attached (see links).
2025-11-18: Prototype v1 uploaded — grid uses named areas and clamp() widths; initial container-query demo added to the Figma prototype. Shared with Eng (ENG-21011) for feasibility.

2025-11-22: Eng notes — older Safari (14.x) has nested overflow clipping. Decided to add small JS shim: on mount, compute stacking contexts and move fixed controls to top-level portal when necessary. Engineering estimates ~3 dev days for shim + tests.

2025-11-25: Design review with PM and Accessibility (Liam Patel). Feedback: ensure keyboard focus order in stacked modals and add visible focus ring exceptions for transformed elements. Added a11y checklist to acceptance criteria.

2025-11-28: Revised prototype v2 — replaced position:sticky in charts with CSS transforms for header behavior, added a collapsed-legend mode for narrow widths to reduce reflow. Cross-browser QA found a jitter in zoom interactions in Firefox; filed ENG follow-up.
2025-12-01: Visual regression tests configured (Percy) for 6 breakpoints + modal stack states. Baseline capture completed.
2025-12-03: PR opened for design token updates and responsive utility classes (see links). Marked In Review pending ENG fixes for Safari clipping and a11y keyboard order validation.
